The *Sāriputta Sutta* (Ud 4.7; PTS Ud 43) is a short discourse located in the fourth chapter of the *Udāna* (*Khuddaka Nikāya*), depicting the Venerable Sāriputta absorbed in meditation. The text sets the narrative context for an inspired utterance (*udāna*) uttered by the Buddha on his disciple's mindful composure. Although several discourses in the Pali Canon share the title *Sāriputta Sutta*, search hits in secondary scholarship refer either to the discourse of that name in the *Aṭṭhakavagga* of the *Sutta Nipāta* (Sn 4.16, also known as the *Upatissapañha*) or to a homonymous discourse in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, leaving this *Udāna* discourse unexamined in the provided literature dossier.

 These include the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 4, UVS 4), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 4), Chinese translations (T 210.2, T 212.4, T 212.5), and a resembling verse in T 213.4. Further canonical parallels are identified in the *Theragāthā* (Thag 1.68, *Ekudāniyattheragāthā*), the Vinaya *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Bu-Vb Pc 22), and Turfan and Gilgit manuscript fragments of the Sanskrit Sarvāstivāda and Mūlasarvāstivāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*.
